subject: thm-fitting-subgroup-contains-its-centralizer-in-a-finite-solvable-group
subclass_note: Craven's Theorem 2.13 (Philip Hall: C_G(F(G)) <= F(G) for soluble G) was declined `deferred` with the reason 'belongs to the soluble-group structure theory and requires an abelian-normal-subgroup argument unused by this pair', and NO destination page id. Both halves fail the standing rules: dropping a result for want of a lemma that could have been written is not a permitted disposition (owner, 2026-08-11), and a decline with no home is indistinguishable from a silent drop. The hole was also structurally visible: Craven's declared harvest range is 'Theorem 2.11 through Proposition 2.14', and 2.11, 2.12 and 2.14 are all `included` — 2.13 was the only decline inside a fully harvested block, on the very page that defines F(G) and proves it is the largest normal nilpotent subgroup. Every dependency the proof needs was already published and in this page's closure. Overturned and BUILT at step 9, as four items: def-centralizer-of-a-subgroup (the library had only the element centralizer C_G(x)), lem-centralizer-of-a-normal-subgroup-is-normal, lem-nontrivial-normal-subgroup-of-a-solvable-group-has-an-abelian-normal-subgroup, and the theorem itself. Statement narrowed to FINITE solvable because the library's Fitting subgroup is a finite-group notion; provenance.statement is ai-altered for that reason.

prevention.ref: A decline with no page id and no item id in its reason is mechanically detectable: coverage-checklist already requires a reason for `deferred`/`out-of-scope`, and could additionally require that the reason contain a page id from plan-spec.json or an item id on disk. 89 of this run's 168 declines name neither.

evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.13, for soluble G the Fitting subgroup contains its centralizer

subject: ex-the-group-action-monad-and-its-algebras
subclass_note: Mac Lane CWM section VI.2's group-action example — the algebras for the monad G x (-) on Set are exactly the G-sets — was declined `out-of-scope` to 'the published group-actions development'. That home cannot receive it: `group-actions-and-cayleys-theorem` sits at order 42, monads are not defined until order 365.005, and published pages are not retrofitted. So the named destination guaranteed the result would land nowhere. The split is visible in the same harvest: Riehl Exercise 5.5.iv ('G-sets are monadic over Set') is correctly deferred to MA-4 because it needs Beck's theorem, while the algebra IDENTIFICATION, which needs nothing beyond this page's own definitions, was dropped. Overturned and BUILT at step 9 on the B page as ex-the-group-action-monad-and-its-algebras. Note it is not the writer monad already on the page: ex-the-writer-monad-from-a-monoid is X x M with the multiplication on the right, whose algebras are RIGHT actions.

prevention.ref: A decline whose named home is a PUBLISHED page is checkable: published pages are never retrofitted, so `already-published` naming an item is the only honest disposition pointing at one. A decline citing a published page id without an item id could be a coverage-checklist error.

subject: research/frontier-15-batch-4.coverage.json, Dembo Definition 1.1.36 heading
subclass_note: The harvested heading reads 'Definition 1.1.36, equivalent complement-and-disjoint-union formulation of a lambda-system'. Dembo's Remark, read from the PDF at printed p. 15, does not say that: it offers 'A^c in L whenever A in L, INSTEAD OF requiring that B\A in L whenever A subset B', keeping the increasing-limit clause. That system is not equivalent, and I have a witness checked element by element — on X={1,2,3,4} the family {emptyset,{1},{1,2},{3,4},{2,3,4},X} contains X, is closed under complements, is closed under increasing unions (X is finite, so every chain terminates), and yet {1,2}\{1}={2} is missing. So the source's Remark as printed is wrong, and the harvest silently repaired it into the form that IS equivalent. Two defects in one row, and the harvest's version is the true one. The item built at step 9 proves the complement-and-COUNTABLE-DISJOINT-UNION form, matching the heading rather than the source, with provenance ai-altered on both components and the discrepancy recorded in the step-9 report. This is a faithfulness defect that survived the step-6 harvest audit because the heading is more plausible than the source.

prevention.ref: The step-6b harvest-faithfulness read compares a heading against the source's SECTION; here the heading and the source's sentence differ by one axiom, which needs the sentence itself opened. Nothing mechanical will catch it; what catches it is opening the exact locator, which is what the 6b.0 rule already asks for.

subject: class:4-items
subclass_note: Four declines whose stated reason is false of disk, all of which STAND on substance but were recorded against a claim that is not true, so a reader following the reason would look in the wrong place. (1) batch 2, Crawley-Boevey section 1.3 Snake Lemma: 'belongs to the later homological-algebra development' — it is thm-snake-lemma-for-modules, PUBLISHED on free-modules-and-exact-sequences at order 104, which is earlier than this page's 108 and inside its transitive closure via tensor-products-of-modules; corrected to already-published naming the item. (2) batch 3, Milne Remark 6.4: 'the equivalences among weaker choice principles are treated on order-zorn-and-the-axiom-of-choice' — that page's 21 items are chains, Bourbaki-Witt, Zorn and Zorn<=>AC, and nothing about weaker principles; the equivalences are on filters-and-ultrafilters as rem-choice-strengths and on deferred-set-theory-beyond-choice as rem-halpern-levy-bpi-not-ac, neither in this pair's closure. (3) batch 4, Tao Exercise 1.4.11: assigned to MT-5, but MT-5 is non-measurable-sets-and-the-cost-of-choice; the Lebesgue and null algebras and the elementary algebra are MT-4 lebesgue-measure-on-euclidean-space, and Jordan content is published at order 235. The neighbouring row correctly says MT-4 for elementary sets, so the file contradicted itself. (4) batch 7, Riehl Example 5.1.4(vi): deferred to 'the categorical-graphs track', which does not exist in research/plan-spec.json; the real obstruction is that ex-the-free-category-on-a-quiver is homed on a B page and B pages are leaves, so no A-page item may cite it. All four reasons rewritten against disk; (4) additionally now names an open owner decision on a destination.

prevention.ref: Three of the four are mechanically checkable at step 2: a reason naming a page id could be checked for existence in plan-spec.json, for order relative to the declining page, and — where it names an already-published home — for an item id. The fourth (Milne 6.4) needs a human to open the named page.

subject: class:2-items
subclass_note: Two items whose iff-forward and iff-reverse boundary rows are `not_applicable` reading 'is a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional', on Statements that carry two directions. fs-finite-nilpotent-and-solvable-groups-coincide refutes 'finite nilpotent groups and finite solvable groups are the same', an equality of classes; its own step 1.1 says the forward inclusion holds and only the converse can fail, so the item knows what the rows deny. cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five states 'the groups of order 105 are C_105 and C_5 x (C_7 : C_3) ... exactly two isomorphism classes', which carries an exhaustiveness obligation and a distinctness obligation, both discharged in its step 5.1. FOUND BY: a targeted detector run at step 9 across all seven batch contracts — a `not_applicable` iff row on an item whose title or Statement contains biconditional language — which produced 18 candidates of which 16 were over-fires and these 2 were real. NEITHER CONCEALED A MATHEMATICAL DEFECT: both proofs discharge exactly the obligations the rows deny exist, which is why this is nonfatal and not the frontier-13/14 pattern. All four rows rewritten as `checked` against the steps that actually discharge them. These two are instances of the class recorded open at f15-a-rr-005; repairing them does not close that row.

prevention.ref: The detector is ~30 lines and worth adding to boundary-audit as a fourth `contradicted` signal: flag a not_applicable iff row when the item's title or Statement matches if-and-only-if / iff / 'exactly' / 'are the same' / 'coincide'. Precision was 2/18 on this run's corpus, which is low for a fail-on gate but fine for a candidate list a human reads.
